title: Digital Peer Pressure & Bullying: The Courage to Stand
summary: The digital world of a teenager is filled with invisible pressures: groups bullying someone, dangerous challenges, photos being demanded or leaked. The danger of social media is that it amplifies pressure and makes mistakes permanent and widespread. Talk to your child that the one who remains silent in the face of bullying is a partner in it, and that true courage is to stand, withdraw, or report. Agree on a rule: never send a photo or information that could be used against them, and no matter what mistake happens, your door is open without scandal. Their confidence that they can tell you without you exploding is their first line of defense.
try_this: This week: Ask your child (without interrogation) if they have seen digital bullying and how those around them reacted. Agree on a family 'code word' they can send to you if they find themselves in an embarrassing digital situation and need a way out.
reflection_prompts: Does your child trust that they can tell you about a digital mistake without you exploding? How can you strengthen this trust?
What is your stance, as a role model, on remaining silent about injustice on the internet?
